title: Utility PRDs
description: PRDs for 3-5 standalone utilities selected for testability. Each PRD covers all flags, exit codes, and stream behaviors derived from C source. Utilities: ts, wc, cat, sponge.

title: PRD: ts (timestamp stdin lines)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/VISION.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, moreutils source (ts.c), prd001-testutils.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml

Write the PRD for ts following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. Derive all requirements from the moreutils C source (ts.c). The PRD must cover: reading stdin line by line and prepending a timestamp to each line; the default format string ('%b %e %T'); custom strftime format strings passed as arguments; -s flag (show elapsed time since ts started); -i flag (show incremental time between lines); -r flag (process existing timestamps, convert format); -m flag (use monotonic clock); high-precision sub-second suffixes when format includes %N or %.N. Exit-code contract: exit 0 on clean EOF, propagate non-zero from stdin pipeline signals. Reference binary: gts (Homebrew moreutils). Note in requirements which flags require timestamp normalization in differential tests.
acceptance_criteria: prd004-ts.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. Every flag from ts.c is covered as a numbered requirement. Differential testing normalization is noted for timestamp-containing output.

title: PRD: wc (count lines, words, bytes)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/VISION.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, coreutils source (src/wc.c), prd001-testutils.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd005-wc.yaml

Write the PRD for wc following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. Derive all requirements from the coreutils C source (src/wc.c). The PRD must cover: -l (line count), -w (word count), -c (byte count), -m (character count, locale-dependent), -L (length of longest line); reading from stdin when no files given; reading multiple files and printing a total line; output column alignment when multiple files are present; exit code 0 on success, non-zero on read error. Explicitly note that -m vs -c diverge under multibyte locales and that differential tests must be run with a fixed locale (LC_ALL=C). Reference binary: gwc (Homebrew coreutils).
acceptance_criteria: prd005-wc.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. All five flags are covered. Locale handling for -m is an explicit requirement. Exit-code contract is stated.

title: PRD: cat (concatenate and display files)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/VISION.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, coreutils source (src/cat.c), prd001-testutils.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd006-cat.yaml

Write the PRD for cat following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. Derive all requirements from the coreutils C source (src/cat.c). The PRD must cover: concatenating one or more files to stdout; reading stdin when no files given or when - is passed as a filename; -n (number all output lines); -b (number non-blank lines, overrides -n); -s (squeeze multiple adjacent blank lines to one); -A (equivalent to -vET, show all non-printing characters); -e (equivalent to -vE); -t (equivalent to -vT); -v (display non-printing characters using ^ and M- notation); -E (display $ at end of each line); -T (display TAB as ^I); binary passthrough: cat must not corrupt binary data on non-text files. Exit code: 0 on success, 1 on any read or write error. Reference binary: gcat (Homebrew coreutils).
acceptance_criteria: prd006-cat.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. All flags are covered. Binary passthrough requirement is explicit. Exit-code contract is stated.

title: PRD: sponge (soak stdin and write to file)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/VISION.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, moreutils source (sponge.c), prd001-testutils.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd007-sponge.yaml

Write the PRD for sponge following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. Derive all requirements from the moreutils C source (sponge.c). The PRD must cover: reading all of stdin into memory before opening the output file (this is the core contract: enables 'cmd | sponge file' where file is also cmd's input without truncating it mid-read); writing the buffered content to the named file after stdin closes; -a flag (append to file instead of overwriting); atomic replacement via a temp file and rename so the target is never partially written; writing to stdout when no filename is given (passthrough mode); exit code: 0 on success, non-zero on write failure. Explicitly state the large-input behavior: sponge must handle stdin larger than available memory by spilling to a temp file. Reference binary: gsponge (Homebrew moreutils).
acceptance_criteria: prd007-sponge.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. The soak-before-write contract is the first requirement. Temp-file atomic rename and large-input spill are covered. Exit-code contract is stated.

title: Source Extraction
description: Clone and catalog the four C source repositories (coreutils, moreutils, grep, findutils). Produce a sources catalog and a shared-dependency map that identifies which pkg/ components each utility will need.

title: Clone source repositories and catalog utility locations
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: bootstrap-prompt.md, docs/VISION.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/sources.yaml

Clone the four C source repositories and catalog each utility's location within them. For each utility record: the source file(s), the flag-parsing entry point, where exit-code logic lives, and the Homebrew reference binary name (e.g. gts, gwc, gcat, gsponge, gpee, gls). Repositories to clone:
  - coreutils (ls, cat, cp, mv, wc, du): https://github.com/coreutils/coreutils.git
  - moreutils (ts, sponge, vidir, pee, chronic): https://git.joeyh.name/git/moreutils.git
  - grep (grep, egrep, fgrep): git://git.savannah.gnu.org/grep.git
  - findutils (find, xargs): git://git.savannah.gnu.org/findutils.git

Clone into a local scratch area (e.g. /tmp/sources/). Do not commit the cloned repos. Only commit docs/specs/sources.yaml.
acceptance_criteria: docs/specs/sources.yaml exists and maps every utility in the four repos to its primary source file and Homebrew reference binary name. All 14 utilities are covered.

title: Analyze source and produce shared-dependency map
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/specs/sources.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml

For each of the 14 utilities, analyze the catalogued C source and identify which shared pkg/ components it will need: pkg/testutils (all utilities), pkg/sys (ls, du, find, xargs -- file metadata, signals, terminal), pkg/format (ls, du -- table alignment, ANSI color, unit conversion). Note any shared behavioral patterns not yet reflected in ARCHITECTURE.yaml (e.g. shared exit-code conventions, shared option-parsing idioms). The dependency-map is the input that justifies the scope of each shared component PRD.
acceptance_criteria: docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml exists. Every utility is mapped to the pkg/ components it requires. Justification is given for each shared component in terms of which utilities drive it and what behavior they share.

title: Use Cases
description: Use cases and test suites for the utilities with PRDs. Each use case is a concrete end-to-end execution path. Each test suite validates differential testing against the Homebrew reference binary.

title: Use case + test suite: ts
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml, docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/constitutions/design.yaml (use_case and test_suite format rules)

Files to create:
  - docs/specs/use-cases/rel01.0-uc001-ts.yaml
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.0-uc001-ts.yaml

Write the use case following the use_case format in design.yaml. The use case must describe a concrete end-to-end path: operator runs a log-producing command piped through 'ts' with a format flag; the Go binary and gts are both invoked with the same input; differential testing normalizes the timestamp values and confirms output structure is identical. Touchpoints must reference pkg/testutils (harness), cmd/ts (implementation), and the Human Operator (spec and issue trigger). Success criteria must be checkable: output lines are prefixed, line count matches input, exit code is 0, differential test passes with normalization applied.

Write the test suite following the test_suite format in design.yaml. Test cases must cover: default format (no flags), custom strftime format, -s elapsed mode, -i incremental mode, multi-line stdin, empty stdin. Each test case must state inputs (args, stdin content), normalization applied, and expected outcomes (exit code, output structure). Test suite traces to rel01.0-uc001-ts.
acceptance_criteria: Both YAML files exist and pass mage analyze. Use case test_suite field matches the test suite id. Test suite traces field references the use case id. All ts flags in prd004 appear in at least one test case.

title: Shared Component PRDs
description: PRDs for pkg/testutils, pkg/sys, and pkg/format. Each PRD explains why the component is shared, which utilities drive its requirements, and how each utility uses the shared interface.

title: PRD: pkg/testutils (differential testing harness)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml

Write the PRD for pkg/testutils following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. The PRD must explain why testutils is a shared component (all 14 utilities gate on it; centralizing normalization logic avoids per-utility duplication). Requirements must cover: executing a Go binary and a GNU reference binary with identical stdin, args, and environment; comparing stdout, stderr, and exit code; reporting divergence with the triggering input and both outputs; providing normalization hooks for known acceptable differences (e.g. timestamps in ts, path prefixes in find). Include non-goals: testutils does not build binaries, does not manage Homebrew installation, does not produce test reports beyond go test output.
acceptance_criteria: prd001-testutils.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. PRD lists which utilities use the harness. Normalization hook requirement is explicit.

title: PRD: pkg/sys (syscall abstractions)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, coreutils source (src/ls.c, src/du.c), findutils source (find/find.c, xargs/xargs.c)

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sys.yaml

Write the PRD for pkg/sys following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. The PRD must explain why sys is a shared component: ls, du, find, and xargs all need stat/lstat, device/inode access, and signal handling (SIGPIPE, SIGWINCH, SIGHUP), and Darwin vs Linux divergence is best managed once. For each syscall surface (file metadata, terminal size, signal handling), state which utilities drive it and what each utility needs from it. Requirements must cover: stat and lstat returning file mode, size, mtime, device, inode; terminal width query (for ls column layout); SIGPIPE handling (suppress broken-pipe errors on stdout close); SIGWINCH handling (re-query terminal width on resize).
acceptance_criteria: prd002-sys.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. Each requirement names the utilities that depend on it. Darwin/Linux portability is addressed in requirements or design decisions.

title: PRD: pkg/format (output formatting)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, coreutils source (src/ls.c, src/du.c)

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd003-format.yaml

Write the PRD for pkg/format following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. The PRD must explain why format is a shared component: both ls and du produce tabular output with column alignment, ANSI color for file types, and human-readable size formatting (K/M/G/T), and duplicating this logic across cmd/ packages would produce inconsistent output. For each formatting capability (column alignment, ANSI color, unit conversion), state which utilities drive it and what each utility needs. Requirements must cover: left- and right-aligned column formatting; ANSI escape sequences for file type colors (directory, symlink, executable, device); human-readable size conversion with configurable block size; stripping color when stdout is not a terminal.
acceptance_criteria: prd003-format.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. Each requirement names the utilities that depend on it. Color suppression for non-TTY output is covered.
